week_in_brief: Home values fell in real terms for the 11th straight month while first-time buyers hit a six-year high — and AI search platforms started scraping MLS data without asking.

items.headline: Real Home Values Down 11 Months Running
items.whats_happening: Case-Shiller shows nominal home price growth of just 0.8% year-over-year in April, but when you adjust for 3.8% inflation, real values have been falling for 11 straight months. Regional splits are extreme: Chicago up 6.5%, Seattle down 2.3%. Meanwhile, seller concessions hit 46% this spring — the highest rate since 2019.
items.so_what: Your marketing can't pretend it's still a seller's market. In softening regions, lead with buyer incentives (credits, buydowns, repairs) and stop running urgency campaigns that make you look out of touch with what sellers are actually experiencing.

items.headline: First-Time Buyers Back — And They Want AI Help First
items.whats_happening: First-time buyers now represent 35% of all purchases, the highest share since June 2020, driven by rising inventory and fewer bidding wars. One in five prospective buyers are using AI tools or chatbots for initial home research — and for Gen Z, that number jumps to 32%. They're using AI for affordability estimates, market research, and neighborhood analysis before they ever talk to an agent.
items.so_what: This is a new lead generation channel, and it requires specific work. Agents need visibility in ChatGTT, Gemini, and Perplexity — not just Google. If your agents aren't being cited in AI search results when someone asks "best neighborhoods under $400K in [your city]," you're invisible to the fastest-growing buyer segment.

items.headline: AI Platforms Scraping MLS Data Without Permission
items.whats_happening: ChatGPT, Gemini, Perplexity, and others are now surfacing MLS listings attributed to Zillow and other portals — feeding buyer queries directly into AI environments without MLS authorization or broker control. Zillow launched the first ChatGPT integration in October 2025; Redfin and Realtor.com followed. The mechanism bypasses IDX policy guardrails that have governed MLS data display for 25 years. NAR has deferred enforcement, leaving 580+ MLS to assess compliance independently.
items.so_what: Td`us is a foundational issue for owned lead generation. If AI platforms are scraping your listings through portals without your permission, you're losing control over how your inventory appears and who owns the lead relationship. Push your MLS to clarify authorization rules — and start treating AI visibility as a channel you need to own, not rent.

items.headline: Compass Rolls Out Home Platform to 340,000 Agents
items.whats_happening: Compass is deploying its AI-powered Home Platform to agents at Coldwell Banker Realty, Corcoran, and Sotheby's International Realty — brands it acquired from Anywhere Real Estate. The platform bundles market analysis, buyer prospecting, and listing performance into a unified agent workflow. Compass is calling it the largest tech deployment in residential real estate history.
items.so_what: Compass is betting it can monetize a 340,000-agent network through proprietary data advantages. For regional brokerages, this is your cue: the competitive counterweight is local brand strength, agent autonomy, and the kind of personalized marketing support that national platforms can't replicate at scale.

items.this_weeks_take: The market is softening, the buyer mix is shifting, and AI platforms are scraping your data without asking. This is the week you stop pretending it's 2022 and start building marketing that reflects the market people are actually in.
